title: Industries in the County
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Bring a product and its raw material: a packet of milk and a picture of a cow, sugar and a piece of sugarcane, flour and maize. Name the factory that joins them.

skills.key_step: The child says what an industry makes and from which raw material, keeping raw material and product the right way round.

floor.prerequisite: Relates food items to the animals or plants they come from.
floor.question: Which animal gives us eggs?

representations: a raw material and its product side by side
arrow cards: raw material to product
steps: Say what the factory does to it.
Check the arrow goes from raw material to product.
contexts: a posho mill in the village

board.do: Draw a cow, an arrow and a packet of milk.

board.say: What happens to the milk in the factory?

board.do: Wait for "it is cooled, cleaned and packed".
Write raw material under the cow and product under the packet.
Ask which comes first for sugarcane and sugar.

misconceptions.ask: What is the raw material in a sugar factory?
misconceptions.repair: Use pairs: before the factory and after the factory.
Ask: does this place make something new from something else?

listen_for: No, only big factories are industries
misconceptions.ask: A women's group makes baskets from sisal to sell. Is this an industry?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a big sugar factory and a jaggery mill: both turn sugarcane into a product.

misconceptions.ask: A tea factory buys green tea leaves from farmers. What does it sell?
misconceptions.repair: Show green leaves and a packet of tea side by side.

checks.question: What is the raw material for a posho mill?
Is a shop that sells soap an industry?
checks.answer: No: it sells goods; it does not make them

skills.key_step: The child says who gains from an industry: workers, farmers who sell to it, buyers of its goods and the county.

floor.prerequisite: Names an industry and its product.
floor.question: What does a tea factory make?

representations: a web drawing with the factory in the middle
role cards for a worker, a farmer and a shopper
steps: Ask who sells to it and who buys from it.
contexts: a milk factory buying from farmers
a jua kali workshop making jikos
a bakery selling bread to schools

board.do: Draw a factory in a circle with four lines going out.

board.say: Who is at the end of this line, and what do they get?

board.do: Wait for a worker getting pay.
Write farmer, worker, shopper, county on the lines.

misconceptions.ask: Who gains when a factory opens in a county?
misconceptions.repair: List who works at a milk factory, who sells it the milk and who buys the milk.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a benefit of an industry?
misconceptions.repair: Sort a list into "good for people" and "problem to solve".

listen_for: It does not; it takes their milk
misconceptions.ask: How does a milk factory help dairy farmers?
misconceptions.repair: Draw the milk going to the factory and the money going back to the farmer.

listen_for: Smoke, it shows the factory is busy
misconceptions.ask: Which is a benefit of a factory: jobs, smoke, noise?
misconceptions.repair: Sort cards into "helps people" and "harms people".

checks.question: Give one way a sugar factory helps cane farmers.
checks.answer: It buys their cane so they earn money

checks.question: Which is a benefit of a factory: jobs or noise?

skills.key_step: The child places an industry near its raw material, roads, water and workers and away from homes, and gives the reason.

floor.prerequisite: Says where counties and places are on a described map.
floor.question: The farms are north of the town. Where is the town from the farms?

representations: a described map with farms, a road, a river and houses
a checklist: raw material, road, water, workers
steps: Find the raw material on the map.
Find the road and the water.
Check it is not among the homes.
contexts: a tea factory among tea farms
a fish factory on the lake shore
a quarry beside the main road

board.do: Draw tea farms, a road and a river.
Point at two places: near the farms and far up a hill.
board.say: Where should the tea factory go?

board.do: Wait for a choice and a reason.
Draw the lorry route to each place to show the cost.

listen_for: Because there is no reason, any place does
misconceptions.ask: Why is a sugar factory built near sugarcane farms?
misconceptions.repair: Ask the child to carry a heavy bag a short way and a long way.

misconceptions.ask: Where is the best place for a milk factory?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to fresh milk after a day in the sun.

listen_for: On the far hill, land is cheap
misconceptions.ask: Where should a new milk factory go: next to the dairy farms by the main road, or on a far hill with no road?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how lorries will bring milk to the far hill.

listen_for: In the middle of the houses
misconceptions.ask: Where is the best place for a noisy, smoky factory?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how families would sleep next to the noise and smoke.

checks.question: Why is a sugar factory built near cane farms?
checks.answer: The cane is heavy and spoils, so it is close to carry

checks.question: Give one more thing a factory needs near it besides raw material.
checks.answer: any of: roads, water, workers, power
